paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and accuracy across three metrics: Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 in linear scale, with tick labels spaced at intervals of 0.02. The y-axis represents Accuracy, scaled linearly from 0.0 to 1.0. The blue line with circular markers, labeled “Final Accuracy,” remains consistently high, hovering near 1.0 across the entire range of initial confidence, with slight fluctuations between approximately 0.97 and 1.00. The green line with square markers, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” starts at approximately 0.65, rises to a peak near 0.90 at an initial confidence of 0.97, then declines slightly to around 0.75 at an initial confidence of 1.00. The orange line with diamond markers, labeled “Δ Accuracy,” begins at approximately 0.25, decreases to a low of about 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.95, and then rises again to approximately 0.20 at an initial confidence of 1.00. All three lines are plotted with error bars indicating variability.
